core_methodology: The paper develops a unified theoretical framework to characterize conservation laws (invariants) governing the gradient flow dynamics during the training of modern neural network architectures, including those using GELU, SiLU, SwiGLU activations, multihead attention (with specialized encodings), and MoE configurations. This involves analyzing how the underlying geometry and flow of optimization paths are constrained by the network structure.
data_sources: The paper focuses on the theoretical properties of neural network training dynamics, using synthetic or benchmark datasets typically found in deep learning research (e.g., for image classification or general function approximation) to validate invariants. Direct financial market data is not the primary focus, but the derived principles apply to models trained on financial data.
alpha_potential: This research has indirect but significant relevance. Understanding the conservation laws for advanced architectures (especially Transformers and MoEs) provides fundamental insights into why certain models succeed in learning features, behave robustly, or converge to specific solutions. For high-frequency AI models in quantitative finance, this knowledge can inform regularization techniques, architecture design choices (e.g., choosing optimal activations or attention mechanisms for time-series prediction), and help explain model generalization or failure modes in volatile market environments.
title_cn: 现代神经网络架构的守恒定律
summary_cn: 该研究为现代AI架构（如使用GELU、SiLU、SwiGLU激活函数和多头注意力机制的模型）的梯度流动力学建立了理论框架，揭示了训练过程中的守恒定律。这为量化交易中设计和优化复杂的深度学习模型（尤其是在处理高频或序列数据时）提供了基础理论支撑，有助于提高模型泛化性和稳定性。

title: Functional Equivalence in Attention: A Comprehensive Study with Applications to Linear Mode Connectivity
summary: Neural network parameter spaces are inherently non-injective, as distinct parameter configurations can realize identical functions through functional equivalence. While this symmetry is well understood in classical fully connected and convolutional models, it becomes substantially more intricate in modern attention-based architectures. Existing analyses of multihead attention have largely focused on the vanilla formulation, overlooking positional encodings that fundamentally reshape architectural symmetries. In this work, we provide a formal study of functional equivalence in Transformers with positional encodings. Focusing on the two most widely used variants--sinusoidal and rotary positional encodings (RoPE)--we show that sinusoidal encodings preserve the equivalence structure of vanilla attention, whereas rotary encodings significantly reduce the symmetry group, thereby enhancing expressivity. This offers a principled explanation for the growing prominence of RoPE in practice. We further examine how positional encodings affect linear mode connectivity, and through an alignment algorithm, empirically demonstrate that the presence and variability of connectivity across Transformer settings crucially depend on the positional encoding.
core_methodology: Formal mathematical study of functional equivalence and symmetry groups within Transformer architectures, specifically comparing sinusoidal and Rotary Positional Encodings (RoPE). It investigates architectural symmetries and their impact on model expressivity and connectivity (linear mode connectivity).
data_sources: This paper focuses on the theoretical properties of neural network architectures (Transformers) rather than specific financial market data. The application context implies using time-series or sequence data common in financial forecasting.
alpha_potential: The findings provide a principled understanding of why specific architectural choices (like RoPE) might lead to better performance or more stable training in sequential modeling tasks. In quantitative finance, building superior forecasting models requires robust, high-expressivity architectures. Understanding these theoretical symmetries can guide the design of more efficient and effective Transformers for tasks like time-series prediction, market state classification, or high-frequency order book analysis, potentially leading to improved alpha generation through better sequence modeling.
title_cn: 注意力机制中的函数等价性：一项基于线性模式连通性的综合研究
summary_cn: 本研究深入分析了带有位置编码的Transformer模型中的函数等价性。研究表明，旋转位置编码（RoPE）相比正弦编码能显著降低模型对称性，从而增强表达能力。这一洞察对量化交易中利用Transformer进行金融时间序列建模至关重要，能指导研究人员选择更优的架构组件，以构建性能更可靠、更具信息捕获能力的预测模型，潜在提升信号质量。

title: Monotonic Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: A Theoretical and Empirical Study of Monotonicity as an Inductive Bias
summary: Monotonicity has been a long-running architectural inductive bias for neural networks, motivated by tabular, scientific, and economic settings where outputs are known to respond monotonically to certain inputs. Existing approaches are MLP- or flow-based and lack per-edge functional transparency; the only Kolmogorov--Arnold Network (KAN) variant with monotonicity, MonoKAN, enforces the constraint only on a restricted parameter subset and requires a projection-style training procedure. We close this gap with \textbf{MKAN}, a KAN with hard monotonicity guaranteed for \emph{all} parameter values via exponential reparameterization of B-spline coefficients, positive edge weights, and a monotone base activation. Training reduces to standard unconstrained gradient descent. Our headline theoretical contribution is a \emph{representation-cost} theorem: any $C^K, K >0$ feature extractor inducing a ball-shaped semantic-neighborhood partition admits a monotone realization of the equivalent neighborhood structure at $N' = N^* + k \le 2N^*$, where $k$ is the number of non-monotone coordinates of the original. The bound is architecture-agnostic and gives a principled sizing rule for monotone encoders. Empirically, MKAN is competitive with state-of-the-art monotone NNs on the SMM/ICML-2024 benchmark while being the only method that combines hard unconstrained monotonicity with KAN's per-edge functional transparency; the $2N^*$ prediction is validated in a self-supervised feature-size sweep on four real datasets, and on a controlled monotone-generative dataset MKAN recovers ground-truth factors with substantially higher Spearman alignment than KAN, MLP, and linear baselines.
core_methodology: The paper introduces MKAN, a novel architecture based on Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN) that guarantees hard monotonicity for all parameters through exponential reparameterization, positive edge weights, and a naturally monotone base activation. This allows for standard unconstrained gradient descent training while maintaining functional transparency. A theoretical contribution is the representation-cost theorem providing a principled sizing rule for monotone encoders.
data_sources: The empirical validation uses the SMM/ICML-2024 benchmark and four real-world datasets for self-supervised feature-size sweeping, though the specific nature of the financial data in these benchmarks is not detailed in the abstract.
alpha_potential: The direct application is in building interpretable, constrained, yet powerful non-linear models. In finance, monotonicity constraints are crucial when modeling relationships known to be directional (e.g., return vs. volatility, or factor exposure vs. portfolio performance). MKAN offers superior interpretability (per-edge transparency) compared to standard NNs or flows, which is vital for regulatory compliance and belief validation in quantitative finance. This improved interpretive modeling capability can lead to more robust factor construction or signal generation where input-output directions are assumed.
title_cn: 单调柯氏-阿诺德网络：关于单调性作为归纳偏置的理论与实证研究
summary_cn: 该研究提出了MKAN，一种具有硬性单调性保证的柯氏-阿诺德网络变体。在量化金融中，单调性约束模型的解释性和稳健性至关重要。MKAN结合了KAN的每边功能透明度和可解释性，使其非常适用于构建对金融变量具有已知单调关系的因子模型、风险归因或投资组合选择模型，提供比传统黑盒NN更可靠的洞察。

title: Trustworthy Self-Composable Big-Data-as-a-Service: An LLM-Orchestrated Multi-Agent Framework for Automated Data Engineering, AutoML, MLOps Deployment, and Drift-Aware Lifecycle Optimization
summary: Big-Data-as-a-Service (BDaaS) platforms require re liable automation across data ingestion, cleaning, feature engi neering, model development, deployment, and post-deployment monitoring. However, existing LLM-based data science agents and AutoML systems mainly focus on isolated workflow stages, leaving limited support for lifecycle-level orchestration, artifact governance, human oversight, and drift-aware adaptation. This paper proposes a trustworthy self-composable BDaaS frame work based on LLM-orchestrated multi-agent collaboration. The proposed architecture decomposes the BDaaS lifecycle into specialized agents for data ingestion, data cleaning, feature engineering, AutoML training, model evaluation, MLOps de ployment, monitoring, and drift detection. A central LLM or chestration layer coordinates agent execution, validates interme diate outputs, manages workflow context, and enables dynamic workflow composition. The framework also incorporates shared artifact governance, reproducibility support, human-in-the-loop checkpoints, and drift-aware feedback loops. A prototype-based evaluation is conducted using controlled tabular benchmark datasets with missing values, categorical variables, outliers, class imbalance, and simulated covariate drift. Compared with manual ML, AutoML-only, and single-agent LLM baselines, the pro posed multi-agent BDaaS pipeline achieves competitive predictive performance while improving lifecycle-level reliability, including workflow completion, artifact traceability, deployment readiness, reproducibility, and drift recovery. The results suggest that LLM-orchestrated multi-agent systems can extend conventional AutoML toward trustworthy, adaptive, and production-oriented BDaaS lifecycle automation.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a multi-agent framework orchestrated by a central LLM to automate the entire Big-Data-as-a-Service (BDaaS) lifecycle, including data engineering, feature engineering, AutoML, MLOps deployment, and drift-aware monitoring. It emphasizes self-composition, artifact governance, and human-in-the-loop checkpoints.
data_sources: While the evaluation uses controlled tabular benchmark datasets (implying structured financial data characteristics like missing values, outliers, etc.), the framework is designed to handle generic big data relevant to financial contexts, such as market data feeds, alternative data, or fundamental datasets.
alpha_potential: This research does not propose a direct alpha signal; instead, it provides a robust, automated, and adaptive infrastructure for *creating and maintaining* quantitative trading models. The core value for trading lies in significantly accelerating the R&D cycle, ensuring model deployment reliability, and automatically recovering from concept or covariate drift in live trading environments, which is critical for strategy longevity.
title_cn: 可信赖自组合式大数据即服务：基于LLM编排的多智能体框架，用于自动化数据工程、AutoML、MLOps部署及漂移感知的生命周期优化
summary_cn: 该研究提供了一个强大的、可信赖的自动化框架，利用多智能体和LLM编排，以端到端方式管理量化策略的开发、部署和监控。其核心价值在于通过自动化数据处理、模型生命周期管理和漂移适应性，显著提高量化系统的可靠性和可维护性，加速模型迭代并应对数据环境变化。

title: KANLib -- An Modular, Extensible and Fast Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Implementation
summary: Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) have recently emerged as a promising alternative to traditional multilayer perceptrons by replacing linear weights with learnable univariate functions. Despite their theoretical advantages in interpretability and expressiveness, practical research of KANs remains difficult due to high computational costs and inconsistent feature support across existing frameworks. This paper introduces KANLib, a modular, extensible, and computationally efficient framework for developing and evaluating KAN architectures. KANLib unifies core concepts from existing implementations, including PyKAN, EfficientKAN, and FastKAN, within a consistent software architecture that emphasizes flexibility, feature parity, and high performance. The framework supports two basis function types, adaptive grid rescaling, grid extension, and fine-grained architectural customization while maintaining compatibility with standard PyTorch workflows. Experimental evaluation on the California Housing benchmark demonstrates that KANLib reproduces the predictive behavior of established reference KAN implementations while achieving competitive computational efficiency. Furthermore, the framework enables the exploration of architectural variations beyond standard KAN formulations with only minor impacts on predictive performance. Overall, KANLib provides a robust foundation for future research on scalable and extensible KAN architectures.
core_methodology: The paper introduces KANLib, a library for implementing and efficiently running Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs). KANs replace traditional MLP weights with learnable univariate functions, offering advantages in interpretability over standard deep neural networks.
data_sources: Primarily benchmark datasets like California Housing for model evaluation, but the framework is intended for general application, including financial time series or structured market data.
alpha_potential: KANs offer a potential improvement in model interpretability compared to standard deep learning models, which is valuable for model validation and regulatory compliance in finance. Their increased expressivity might allow for capturing complex, non-linear relationships in market data (e.g., complex order book dynamics or factor interactions) more effectively than standard MLPs, potentially leading to novel alpha signals. However, the implementation itself is a tool, not a strategy. Its direct value comes from enabling better modeling of existing alpha signals.
title_cn: KANLib -- 一个模块化、可扩展和快速的Kolmogorov-Arnold网络实现
summary_cn: KANLib提供了一个高性能、可扩展的框架用于实现Kolmogorov-Arnold网络（KANs）。KANs因其高表示能力和更强的可解释性，有望替代传统神经网络（MLP）来处理复杂的金融时间序列数据或因子建模，从而发现更稳健、更易理解的交易信号。该库的实用性在于为金融应用中的新型深度学习模型研究提供了强大的工程基础。

title: SoftMoE: Soft Differentiable Routing for Mixture-of-Experts in LLMs
summary: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures enable scaling LLM parameters under a fixed inference budget by activating only a small subset of experts via top-$k$ routing. While this preserves causality and suits autoregressive language models, the discrete top-$k$ operator is not differentiable, forcing a fixed number of active experts per input and resulting in inefficient use of computation. We propose SoftMoE, which replaces discrete routing with a truncated soft top-$k$ LapSum relaxation, allowing gradient-based optimization of expert routing. We further parameterize the mean number of active experts per layer and impose a global budget constraint, enabling the model to learn how to allocate expert capacity across layers. SoftMoE remains fully compatible with autoregressive modeling and achieves performance comparable to or better than sparse MoE on language modeling and downstream tasks, while activating significantly fewer experts. Notably, the learned allocation is highly non-uniform, with later layers activating more experts. The source code is publicly available$^\dagger$.
core_methodology: The paper proposes SoftMoE, which replaces traditional discrete top-k routing in Sparse Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models with a soft, differentiable LapSum relaxation. This allows for gradient-based optimization of expert routing decisions and introduces a mechanism to globally control and learn the non-uniform allocation of expert capacity across different layers.
data_sources: Primarily focuses on large language modeling tasks (e.g., language modeling data), not explicit financial market data. However, the optimized architecture can be applied to financial datasets.
alpha_potential: While not a direct trading strategy, SoftMoE offers a significant architectural improvement for building highly efficient and capable AI models. In quantitative finance, this means developing superior prediction models (e.g., market state classification, high-frequency signal extraction, complex derivate pricing) that require massive parameter counts but must operate within strict computational budgets (latency-sensitive environments). The efficiency and optimized capacity allocation could lead to more performant LLM-based agents or predictive features.
title_cn: SoftMoE：用于LLM中稀疏专家混合模型的软可微路由
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种名为SoftMoE的改进专家混合模型路由机制，使用软可微松弛替代离散路由，优化了模型的计算效率和容量分配。对于量化交易而言，这意味着可以构建计算负担更轻、性能更佳的超大规模语言模型（LLM）或基于Transformer架构的预测模型，以处理市场预测、风险评估或信号生成等任务，从而在保持低延迟的同时提升模型性能。

title: LLM Consumer Behavior Theory: Foundations of a Novel Research Field
summary: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as autonomous agents that make consumption decisions on behalf of users. This shift raises fundamental questions for consumer theory, which has traditionally modeled humans as the primary decision-makers. In this paper, we introduce LLM Consumer Behavior Theory, a new field of study concerned with analyzing consumer behavior in agentic markets. Drawing on classical and behavioral economics alongside recent advances in Natural Language Processing, we formalize how human preferences are reflected and acted upon by LLM-based agents, and how agent-level decisions aggregate into market demand. We unify previously fragmented literature on LLM decision-making, human behavior simulation, and preference elicitation under a common economic lens, highlighting where assumptions, such as rationality and heterogeneity, may fail in agentic markets. Rather than providing empirical validation, this paper outlines the scope of LLM consumer behavior and identifies open research questions related to alignment, preference representation, and market dynamics.
core_methodology: Formalizing consumer behavior theory within the context of autonomous LLM agents making consumption decisions, integrating classical/behavioral economics with NLP concepts. It focuses on how human preferences are represented and acted upon by LLM agents.
data_sources: Conceptual frameworks derived from economics, behavioral science, and LLM decision-making paradigms, rather than direct market data.
alpha_potential: This paper provides a macroeconomic/behavioral framework for understanding how LLM-driven agents influence market demand and resource allocation. While not a direct trading signal generator, it is highly relevant for understanding systemic shifts in market structure (e.g., asset selection, allocation) driven by advanced AI agents. Hedge funds or asset managers deploying LLM agents for investment research or execution need to understand these dynamics to predict aggregated demand shifts.
title_cn: LLM 消费者行为理论：一个新兴研究领域的基石
summary_cn: 该研究提出了LLM消费者行为理论，分析了自主LLM代理如何在市场中代表人类做出消费决策。对于量化交易而言，理解LLM如何聚合和影响市场需求至关重要，这有助于预测受AI代理驱动的宏观需求变化和市场结构演变，为制定适应agentic市场的投资策略提供理论基础。

title: Learning Fair Pareto-Optimal Policies in Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning
summary: Fairness is an important aspect of decision-making in multi-objective reinforcement learning (MORL), where policies must ensure both optimality and equity across multiple, potentially conflicting objectives. While single-policy MORL methods can learn fair policies for fixed user preferences using welfare functions such as the generalized Gini welfare function (GGF), they fail to provide the diverse set of policies necessary for dynamic or unknown user preferences. To address this limitation, we formalize the fair optimization problem in multi-policy MORL, where the goal is to learn a set of Pareto-optimal policies that ensure fairness across all possible user preferences. Our key technical contributions are threefold: (1) We show that for concave, piecewise-linear welfare functions (e.g., GGF), fair policies remain in the convex coverage set (CCS), which is an approximated Pareto front for linear scalarization. (2) We demonstrate that non-stationary policies, augmented with accrued reward histories, and stochastic policies improve fairness by dynamically adapting to historical inequities. (3) We propose three novel algorithms, which include integrating GGF with multi-policy multi-objective Q-Learning (MOQL), state-augmented multi-policy MOQL for learning non-statoinary policies, and its novel extension for learning stochastic policies. We evaluate our algorithms across various domains and compare our methods against the state-of-the-art MORL baselines. The empirical results show that our methods learn a set of fair policies that accommodate different user preferences.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on Multi-Objective Reinforcement Learning (MORL) and introduces methods to learn a set of Pareto-optimal policies that balance multiple, potentially conflicting objectives while ensuring fairness across potential user preferences. Key contributions include using the convex coverage set (CCS) approximation for piecewise-linear welfare functions (like the generalized Gini welfare function, GGF), and employing non-stationary and stochastic policies augmented with reward histories to dynamically adapt fairness criteria. Novel algorithms integrate GGF with MOQL (Multi-policy Multi-objective Q-Learning).
data_sources: The paper does not specify financial data sources, instead focusing on algorithmic frameworks evaluated across various domains. For trading, this would imply a framework applicable to environments where multiple objectives (e.g., profit maximization, risk minimization, fairness/drawdown limits) must be balanced, likely using time-series market data for rewards/states.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is moderate. While the paper doesn't present a trading strategy, its framework for learning a *set* of diverse, fair, and optimal policies is highly applicable to complex portfolio management. In trading, objectives often conflict (e.g., maximizing return vs. minimizing Volatility/Tail Risk/Drawdown). This MORL framework allows a trader to dynamically select a policy from the learned set based on current market perception of risk tolerance or to generate a diverse, robust portfolio allocation that satisfies specific fairness/risk constraints beyond simple mean-variance optimization.
title_cn: 在多目标强化学习中学习公平帕累托最优策略
summary_cn: 该研究提出了多目标强化学习（MORL）框架，旨在学习一组平衡了多目标冲突（如收益与风险/公平性）且满足不同用户偏好的帕累托最优策略集。这对于构建在复杂市场环境下需要同时满足多种约束（如最大化收益、限制特定风险指标或保证投资组合间的公平分配）的投资组合优化策略具有重要潜力。通过学习一系列动态调整的策略，可适应不断变化的市场偏好。

title: Kolmogorov Regression for Robust Diffusion Policies
summary: Finite-dimensional (FD) diffusion policies exhibit temporal drift owing to discretization artifacts that degrade long-horizon performance (when deployed on physical systems). We introduce a backward Kolmogorov equation that lifts diffusion policies to a Cameron-Martin space -- a subset of the Hilbert space. Essentially, replacing stochastic score matching with a deterministic boundary-value PDE problem. Our core innovation thrives on Gaussian measure theory whereupon the diffusion noise covariance operator is realized from a colored noise distribution which prescribes a notion of regularity on samples from the model at inference time. We train the diffusion model with a derived precision-weighted Cameron- Martin loss and a Kolmogorov residual is introduced as a PDE diagnostic during inference. These substitutions yield (i) convergence guarantees where the bound's constants depend on the effective rank of the kernel rather than action dimension, (ii) improved trajectory regularity via spectral weighting, and (iii) a deterministic failure detector without reward signals. Validation across two application domains demonstrates substantial improvements: on the PushT manipulation benchmark, the Cameron-Martin loss achieves a 17% improvement in maximum episode reward (0.95 vs. 0.78 for MSE) and 67.6% reduction in inter-step drifts during inference via the introduced residual magnitude. Similarly, on a 6-station manufacturing line with constant work-in-process (CONWIP) flow control, we achieve 28.4% lower RMSE than classical LSTM baselines; a high starvation-event recall (1.0 in test cycles), and effective bottleneck identification (Precision@1 = 1.0 in test set, 13x signal-to-noise ratio). We then certify the dispatch policies with Hamilton-Jacobi reachability theory which reduces deadlock events by 96% compared to uncontrolled dispatch over 100 simulated runs (351 events prevented).
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel framework, Kolmogorov Regression, to address temporal drift and sub-optimal long-horizon performance in finite-dimensional (FD) diffusion policies by lifting them to a Cameron-Martin space via a backward Kolmogorov equation. This replaces standard stochastic score matching with a deterministic boundary-value PDE problem, using Gaussian measure theory and colored noise. The training involves a precision-weighted Cameron-Martin loss and a Kolmogorov residual diagnostic for inference, leading to convergence guarantees dependent on effective rank rather than action dimension.
data_sources: The methodology is validated on physical control benchmarks (PushT manipulation, CONWIP flow control) rather than direct financial market data. However, the underlying principles of robust control and policy optimization are directly transferable to financial time series prediction and optimal execution.
alpha_potential: While the paper applies the method to robotics and manufacturing flow control, the core advancement lies in creating highly robust, regularization-aware diffusion policies that mitigate drift and exhibit strong convergence properties. In finance, this robust control can be applied to high-frequency trading (HFT) execution algorithms, dynamic optimal portfolio allocation under high noise environments, or robust policy learning for mean-reversion strategies. The deterministic failure detector offers a valuable tool for real-time risk management in automated trading systems.
title_cn: Kolmogorov回归用于鲁棒扩散策略
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于Kolmogorov方程和Cameron-Martin空间来改进扩散策略鲁棒性的新方法，解决了有限维扩散策略的时间漂移问题。其核心创新是将随机分数匹配替换为确定性的偏微分方程（PDE）边界值问题，提高了策略的长期性能和正则性。虽然验证于物理系统，该方法可迁移至高频交易执行、动态投资组合优化等领域，特别是其引入的确定性故障检测机制，对提升交易系统风险控制能力具有显著潜力。

title: Fixed-Point Reasoners: Stable and Adaptive Deep Looped Transformers
summary: Looped architectures provide an inductive bias toward learning step-by-step procedures for tasks that require compositional reasoning. The number of effective layers reached by looping determines the quality of the solution these models find. Like deep architectures, looped architectures are prone to a signal propagation problem induced by depth as the halting decision is postponed. In this paper, we address this signal propagation issue using pre-norm layers and residual scaling. Building on these architectural modifications, we propose FPRM, a Transformer-based Fixed-Point Reasoning Model that uses fixed-point convergence as an end-to-end halting mechanism in a looped architecture. We show that fixed-point halting allows FPRM to adapt its compute to task difficulty. FPRM is effective on common reasoning benchmarks, namely Sudoku, Maze, state-tracking, and ARC-AGI.
core_methodology: The paper introduces Fixed-Point Reasoning Models (FPRM), a Transformer architecture employing looped layers that halts computation iteratively based on fixed-point convergence. This allows the model to adaptively self-regulate the depth of computation required for a given input, addressing the signal propagation issues common in deep recurrent models.
data_sources: The paper tests the model on generalized reasoning benchmarks (Sudoku, Maze, state-tracking, ARC-AGI), not specific financial market data. However, the methodology could be applied to structured time-series or sequence data in finance, such as order book dynamics or stylized market processes.
alpha_potential: The primary value lies in efficient, adaptive computation for sequential decision-making tasks. In quantitative finance, this could be leveraged for tasks requiring iterative planning or deep reasoning over complex sequential inputs, such as multi-step optimal trade execution (where computation must adapt to market shifts) or complex regime detection where the required depth of analysis varies significantly per observation. The fixed-point halting mechanism offers potential for significant efficiency gains over standard fixed-depth Transformers when reasoning complexity is heterogenous.
title_cn: 固定点推理器：稳定且自适应的深度循环Transformer
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于循环结构和固定点收敛作为停止机制的Transformer模型（FPRM）。在金融领域，该方法的核心价值在于其自适应计算能力，可用于需要迭代推理的复杂任务，如根据市场状态变化动态调整分析深度的最优执行策略或多步序列决策建模。这有望提高模型的计算效率和推理准确性。

title: Beyond IGO-Flow: Toward Convergence Analysis of IGO in Continuous Spaces
summary: Information-Geometric Optimization (IGO) provides a unified framework for black-box optimization by interpreting the adaptation of a search distribution as a natural gradient update. Despite its conceptual importance, the convergence theory of IGO remains limited: most existing results concern continuous-time idealizations such as the IGO flow, rather than discrete-time updates with non-infinitesimal learning rates. In this paper, we study discrete-time IGO in continuous spaces, formulated as natural gradient updates in the expectation-parameter coordinates of an exponential family. In particular, we analyze IGO over the multivariate Gaussian family on strongly convex quadratic objective functions. Our analysis covers a setting that simultaneously incorporates full covariance adaptation, a fixed positive learning rate, and quantile-based weights. In this setting, we prove that the covariance matrix converges to the zero matrix. We further show that the mean vector converges to the global optimum, provided that the condition number of the appropriately scaled covariance matrix is bounded at sufficiently frequent iterations. These results advance the convergence theory of IGO and help bridge the gap between the mathematical theory of IGO and practical covariance-adaptive search methods such as CMA-ES.
core_methodology: The paper focuses on Information-Geometric Optimization (IGO), specifically analyzing its convergence properties in discrete-time settings using natural gradient updates within exponential families. It proves convergence results for IGO applied to strongly convex quadratic objective functions, specifically addressing full covariance adaptation. This theoretical advancement is crucial for improving optimization algorithms like CMA-ES (Covariance Matrix Adaptation Evolution Strategy).
data_sources: Theoretical focus on strongly convex quadratic objective functions; does not use specific market data. However, the algorithmic improvements are intended for application in black-box optimization problems often encountered in quantitative finance.
alpha_potential: The direct alpha potential is low as this is a theoretical optimization paper. However, the improved convergence and robustness of discrete-time IGO—which underpins adaptive search methods like CMA-ES—have significant indirect value. Better optimization guarantees for these methods translate directly to more reliable and efficient portfolio construction, hyperparameter tuning for ML models, and potentially complex high-dimensional strategy discovery where the objective function is non-differentiable or noisy.
title_cn: 超越IGO流：连续空间中IGO收敛性分析的探索
summary_cn: 该论文深入研究了离散时间信息几何优化（IGO）的收敛性，这直接关系到自适应搜索方法（如CMA-ES）的性能和鲁棒性。优化理论的进步有助于金融领域中非光滑或黑盒问题的稳健求解，例如复杂投资组合优化、风险模型校准或强化学习的超参数调优，从而间接提升交易策略的开发效率和性能。

title: A Diffusion Approximation for Temporal-Difference Learning with Linear Features under Markovian Noise
summary: Temporal difference (TD) learning with linear function approximation is a core method for policy evaluation. Its classical continuous-time description is an ordinary differential equation (ODE), which captures the asymptotic mean dynamics but neglects stochastic fluctuations determining the error floor. We introduce a stochastic differential equation (SDE) approximation for linear TD(0) under Markovian noise. The resulting model distinguishes the contraction dynamics governed by the projected Bellman operator from the influence of Markovian sampling. As a consequence, the model explains the constant-stepsize error floor through the interaction between Markovian long-run covariance and the contraction geometry of the projected Bellman operator.
core_methodology: This paper introduces a diffusion approximation (SDE model) for Temporal-Difference (TD) learning with linear features under Markovian noise. It refines the traditional ODE framework by accounting for stochastic fluctuations, specifically explaining the constant-stepsize error floor through the interaction of Markovian long-run covariance and the contraction dynamics of the projected Bellman operator.
data_sources: The methodology is based on theoretical model analysis, primarily requiring time-series data amenable to Reinforcement Learning setups, such as simulated or real trading environments where policy evaluation and function approximation are applicable (e.g., sequential market data for state/action/reward sequences).
alpha_potential: While this paper is highly theoretical, it addresses fundamental performance limitations (the 'error floor') in linear TD learning when applied in non-Markovian or noisy environments typical of financial markets. Improved understanding and mitigation of instability/error bounds in value function approximation via TD methods can lead to more robust and reliable Reinforcement Learning agents for dynamic trading execution, optimal control, and portfolio management where policy evaluation is critical. It’s a foundational step for better RL-based trading systems.
title_cn: 线性特征下马尔可夫噪声中时序差分学习的扩散近似
summary_cn: 本文提出了一个用于线性TD学习的随机微分方程（SDE）近似模型，用以在存在马尔可夫噪声的环境中更准确地评估策略。该研究有助于理解和解决金融市场中强化学习算法（如基于TD的方法）固定步长下的误差上限问题，从而提升基于RL的交易执行和资产管理策略的稳健性和收敛性。

title: Variational autoencoders with latent high-dimensional steady geometric flows for dynamics
summary: We develop Riemannian approaches to variational autoencoders (VAEs) for PDE-type ambient data with regularizing geometric latent dynamics, which we refer to as VAE-DLM, or VAEs with dynamical latent manifolds. We redevelop the VAE framework such that manifold geometries, subject to our geometric flow, embedded in Euclidean space are learned in the intermediary latent space developed by encoders and decoders. By tailoring the geometric flow in which the latent space evolves, we induce latent geometric properties of our choosing, which are reflected in empirical performance. We reformulate the traditional evidence lower bound (ELBO) loss with a considerate choice of prior. We develop a linear geometric flow with a steady-state regularizing term. This flow requires only automatic differentiation of one time derivative, and can be solved in moderately high dimensions in a physics-informed approach, allowing more expressive latent representations. We discuss how this flow can be formulated as a gradient flow, and maintains entropy away from metric singularity. This, along with an eigenvalue penalization condition, helps ensure the manifold is sufficiently large in measure, nondegenerate, and a canonical geometry, which contribute to a robust representation. Our methods focus on the modified multi-layer perceptron architecture with tanh activations for the manifold encoder-decoder. We demonstrate, on our datasets of interest, our methods perform at least as well as the traditional VAE, and oftentimes better. Our methods can outperform this and a VAE endowed with our proposed architecture, frequently reducing out-of-distribution (OOD) error between 15% to 35% on select datasets. We highlight our method on ambient PDEs whose solutions maintain minimal variation in late times. We provide empirical justification towards how we can improve robust learning for external dynamics with VAEs.
core_methodology: The paper introduces VAE-DLM (Variational Autoencoders with Dynamical Latent Manifolds), which uses Riemannian geometry and geometric flows to regularize the latent space of VAEs. It aims to learn structured, geometric latent representations for time-series or ambient data by modifying the ELBO loss and employing a linear geometric flow with steady-state regularization. This results in more robust and geometrically constrained latent representations.
data_sources: The abstract mentions 'ambient data' and 'datasets of interest,' specifically citing application to ambient PDEs whose solutions maintain minimal variation in late times. In a financial context, this would likely be applied to time-series data like price series, volatility surfaces, or high-dimensional state vectors.
alpha_potential: The improved robustness and reduced Out-of-Distribution (OOD) error (15%-35%) make VAE-DLM a potentially powerful tool for time-series forecasting and representation learning in finance. Enhanced representation learning can lead to better feature engineering for predictive models (e.g., for next-day returns or volatility). The method's ability to capture complex, low-dimensional geometric structures in high-dimensional financial data could improve signal extraction, especially in modeling regimes or capturing subtle state transitions, which could translate into more robust alpha signals or better risk modeling.
title_cn: 具有潜在高维稳定几何流的变分自编码器
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种基于黎曼几何的VAE变体（VAE-DLM），通过在潜在空间中引入稳定的几何流来增强时间序列数据的表征能力。相比传统VAE，该方法显著降低了模型在分布外数据的误差（15%-35%）。在量化交易中，这可用于构建更鲁棒的金融时间序列（如价格、波动率）的低维嵌入特征，提升因子模型的预测精度和策略的泛化能力。

title: AnomalyMatch: Discovering Rare Objects of Interest with Semi-supervised and Active Learning
summary: Anomaly detection in large datasets is essential in astronomy and computer vision. However, due to a scarcity of labelled data, it is often infeasible to apply supervised methods to anomaly detection. We present AnomalyMatch, an anomaly detection framework combining the semi-supervised FixMatch algorithm using EfficientNet classifiers with active learning. AnomalyMatch is tailored for large-scale applications and integrated into the ESA Datalabs science platform. In this method, we treat anomaly detection as a binary classification problem and efficiently utilise limited labelled and abundant unlabelled images for training. We enable active learning via a user interface for verification of high-confidence anomalies and correction of false positives. Evaluations on the GalaxyMNIST astronomical dataset and the miniImageNet natural-image benchmark under severe class imbalance display strong performance. Starting from five to ten labelled anomalies, we achieve an average AUROC of 0.96 (miniImageNet) and 0.89 (GalaxyMNIST), with respective AUPRC of 0.82 and 0.77. After three active learning cycles, anomalies are ranked with 76% (miniImageNet) to 94% (GalaxyMNIST) precision in the top 1% of the highest-ranking images by score. We compare to the established Astronomaly software on selected 'odd' galaxies from the 'Galaxy Zoo- The Galaxy Challenge' dataset, achieving comparable performance with an average AUROC of 0.83. Our results underscore the exceptional utility and scalability of this approach for anomaly discovery, highlighting the value of specialised approaches for domains characterised by severe label scarcity
core_methodology: The core methodology, AnomalyMatch, leverages a semi-supervised approach (FixMatch) with an EfficientNet classifier, enhanced by active learning. It treats anomaly detection as a binary classification problem, efficiently using scarce labelled data alongside abundant unlabelled data. Active learning is incorporated via a user interface for verifying and correcting high-confidence anomaly predictions.
data_sources: The paper uses astronomical image datasets (GalaxyMNIST, Galaxy Zoo) for demonstration. In a financial context, this implies applying the methodology to large, unbalanced datasets where 'anomalies' (e.g., rare market events, novel patterns, or data artifacts) are sparsely labeled.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on astronomical objects, the underlying methodology is highly relevant for detecting rare, high-impact events in financial time series or market microstructure data. This can be adapted to identify regime shifts, liquidity crises, flash crash precursors, or extremely rare trading opportunities (alpha signals) in high-frequency/alternative datasets where labelled examples of these events are scarce. The active learning component is vital for efficiently training models on these rare observations.
title_cn: AnomalyMatch：利用半监督和主动学习发现值得关注的罕见目标
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种结合FixMatch半监督学习和主动学习的异常检测框架，适用于标签稀缺的大规模数据集。该方法可应用于金融领域，用于识别罕见的市场异常事件、洗盘信号或潜在的金融风险事件。通过主动学习高效地利用少量标注数据，有助于构建对市场极端事件更具鲁棒性和适应性的交易或风险模型。

title: Critique of World Model: A Generative Latent Prediction Architecture for World Modeling
summary: World Model, the algorithmic simulator of the real-world environment which biological agents experience and act upon, has been an emerging topic in recent years due to the rising need to develop virtual agents with artificial (general) intelligence. There has been much discussion on what a world model really is, how to build it, how to use it, and how to evaluate it. In this essay, starting from the imagination in the famed Sci-Fi classic Dune, and drawing inspiration from the concept of ``hypothetical thinking'' in psychology literature, we argue the primary goal of a world model to be {\it simulating all actionable possibilities of the real world for purposeful reasoning and acting}. We examine the key design dimensions of world modeling: data, representation, architecture, learning objective, and usage, surveying existing approaches and analyzing their tradeoffs. Building on this examination, we propose a new Generative Latent Prediction (GLP) architecture for a general-purpose world model, based on stateful, hierarchical, multi-level, and mixed continuous/discrete representations, and a generative and self-supervised learning framework, with an outlook of a Physical, Agentic, and Nested (PAN) AGI system enabled by such a model.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a Generative Latent Prediction (GLP) architecture aiming to simulate the real world for purposeful reasoning. This involves stateful, hierarchical, multi-level representations and a generative, self-supervised learning framework, contrasting with existing world modeling approaches.
data_sources: The paper discusses world models generally, suggesting inputs relevant to simulating complex environments, which in a financial context would translate to time-series market data, order book data, economic indicators, and potentially unstructured data for context.
alpha_potential: While the paper is explicitly focused on AGI and general world modeling, the core concept of building a generative simulator capable of predicting 'actionable possibilities' (i.e., future states based on actions) is highly relevant to reinforcement learning in finance. A functional world model could be used to train highly sophisticated trading agents in a simulated market environment, allowing for exploration of complex strategies or portfolio allocations that are too risky or time-consuming to test in live markets. It offers a framework for advanced agentic trading systems.
title_cn: 世界模型的批判：一种用于世界建模的生成式潜在预测架构
summary_cn: 该论文提出了生成式潜在预测（GLP）架构，旨在构建能够模拟现实世界并支持目的性推理的通用模型。虽然主要面向通用人工智能，但其核心的复杂环境模拟和预测能力可应用于金融领域，特别是在强化学习驱动的交易代理训练中，用于探索和优化复杂的投资策略和资产配置，从而发现潜在的交易信号和风险管理机制。

title: Geodesic Calculus on Implicitly Defined Latent Manifolds
summary: Latent manifolds of autoencoders provide low-dimensional representations of data, which can be studied from a geometric perspective. We propose to describe these latent manifolds as implicit submanifolds of some ambient latent space. Based on this, we develop tools for a discrete Riemannian calculus approximating classical geometric operators. These tools are robust against inaccuracies of the implicit representation often occurring in practical examples. To obtain a suitable implicit representation, we propose to learn an approximate projection onto the latent manifold by minimizing a denoising objective. This approach is independent of the underlying autoencoder and supports the use of different Riemannian geometries on the latent manifolds. The framework in particular enables the computation of geodesic paths connecting given end points and shooting geodesics via the Riemannian exponential maps on latent manifolds. We evaluate our approach on various autoencoders trained on synthetic and real data.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a discrete Riemannian calculus framework for analyzing data implicitly represented on learned latent manifolds (e.g., from autoencoders). This involves learning robust projections onto the manifold and defining geometric operators like geodesic paths and exponential maps directly on this implicitly defined surface.
data_sources: The evaluation uses synthetic and real data to test the autoencoder reconstruction and manifold analysis. While not explicitly financial data, the methodology is applicable to high-dimensional financial time series or alternative datasets encoded into latent spaces (e.g., proprietary sentiment data, order book snapshots, complex macroeconomic features).
alpha_potential: The primary value lies in providing a mathematically robust way to analyze the geometry of complex, high-dimensional data representations learned by deep learning models. In trading, this could enhance strategy development by: 1. **Improved Feature Engineering:** Identifying meaningful, low-dimensional paths (geodesics) through complex market states defined in the latent space. 2. **State Transition Modeling:** Understanding the natural, shortest paths between different market regimes, which can inform regime-switching models or optimal execution (e.g., path planning for large orders). 3. **Anomaly Detection:** Deviations from expected geodesic behavior in the latent space might signal market dislocations.
title_cn: 隐式定义的潜在流形上的测地线微积分
summary_cn: 该研究开发了在深度学习自动编码器提取的隐式潜在流形上进行几何分析的工具。在量化交易中，该方法可用于更精确地理解复杂高维金融数据（如订单簿或宏观因子）的潜在结构。通过计算流形上的测地线，可以识别出市场状态间的自然演变路径，为开发更鲁棒的量化策略、 regime 切换模型或高维度特征工程提供新的几何视角。

title: Softmax as Linear Attention in the Large-Prompt Regime: a Measure-based Perspective
summary: Softmax attention is a central component of transformer architectures, yet its nonlinear structure poses significant challenges for theoretical analysis. We develop a unified, measure-based framework for studying single-layer softmax attention under both finite and infinite prompts. For i.i.d. Gaussian inputs, we lean on the fact that the softmax operator converges in the infinite-prompt limit to a linear operator acting on the underlying input-token measure. Building on this insight, we establish non-asymptotic concentration bounds for the output and gradient of softmax attention, quantifying how rapidly the finite-prompt model approaches its infinite-prompt counterpart, and prove that this concentration remains stable along the entire training trajectory in general in-context learning settings with sub-Gaussian tokens. In the case of in-context linear regression, we use the tractable infinite-prompt dynamics to analyze training at finite prompt length. Our results allow optimization analyses developed for linear attention to transfer directly to softmax attention when prompts are sufficiently long, showing that large-prompt softmax attention inherits the analytical structure of its linear counterpart. This, in turn, provides a principled and broadly applicable toolkit for studying the training dynamics and statistical behavior of softmax attention layers in large prompt regimes.
core_methodology: The research analyzes the convergence of Softmax Attention, a core component of Transformers, to a linear operator in the 'large-prompt' (long sequence) regime using a measure-based framework. It establishes concentration bounds and transfers analytical results from linear attention to softmax attention under specific conditions. This simplifies the analysis of large, over-parameterized transformer models.
data_sources: The analysis focuses on theoretical properties concerning i.i.d. Gaussian inputs and general in-context learning settings (sub-Gaussian tokens), rather than specific market data. However, the insights are applicable when using time-series financial data as token sequences.
alpha_potential: While the paper is theoretical, it directly addresses the computational and analytical bottleneck of using large Transformers in finance (e.g., for long-horizon time-series forecasting or complex agent environments). By showing that large-prompt softmax attention behaves similarly to simpler linear attention, it paves the way for leveraging established, efficient linear methods for training or inference on high-dimensional financial sequence data, potentially improving stability and interpretability in forecasting models.
title_cn: 大提示语境下Softmax作为线性注意力的一种度量视角
summary_cn: 该研究揭示了在长序列（大提示）输入下，Transformer中的Softmax注意力机制在数学上收敛于线性注意力。这为使用更稳定和可分析的线性模型工具来研究金融时间序列预测中的大型Transformer动态提供了理论基础，有助于提高长序列金融建模的效率和可解释性。

title: Does the Data Processing Inequality Reflect Practice? On the Utility of Low-Level Tasks
summary: The data processing inequality is an information-theoretic principle stating that the information content of a signal cannot be increased by processing the observations. In particular, it suggests that there is no benefit in enhancing the signal or encoding it before addressing a classification problem. This assertion can be proven to be true for the case of the optimal Bayes classifier. However, in practice, it is common to perform "low-level" tasks before "high-level" downstream tasks despite the overwhelming capabilities of modern deep neural networks. In this paper, we aim to understand when and why low-level processing can be beneficial for classification. We present a comprehensive theoretical study of a binary classification setup, where we consider a classifier that is tightly connected to the optimal Bayes classifier and converges to it as the number of training samples increases. We prove that for any finite number of training samples, there exists a pre-classification processing that improves the classification accuracy. We also explore the effect of class separation, training set size, and class balance on the relative gain from this procedure. We support our theory with an empirical investigation of the theoretical setup. Finally, we conduct an empirical study where we investigate the effect of denoising and encoding on the performance of practical deep classifiers on benchmark datasets. Specifically, we vary the size and class distribution of the training set, and the noise level, and demonstrate trends that are consistent with our theoretical results.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the Data Processing Inequality (DPI) in the context of classification, proposing that pre-processing (low-level tasks like denoising or encoding) can improve classification accuracy for a finite number of samples, even when the optimal Bayes classifier converges to the same result asymptotically. It involves theoretical proofs supported by empirical tests on benchmark datasets involving varying noise levels and training set sizes.
data_sources: Benchmark machine learning datasets are used for empirical validation. For finance, this implies sensor or market data that requires feature engineering or cleaning before final prediction (e.g., noisy time series, high-frequency limit order book data).
alpha_potential: The findings suggest that standard deep learning pipelines, which often skip explicit low-level feature engineering (like specialized denoising or encoding), might be sub-optimal when training data is scarce or noisy (which is common in financial modeling). An alpha strategy could involve explicitly designing preprocessing steps (denoising, filtering, specialized encoding) that enhance the signal strength before feeding it into a predictive deep learning model (e.g., a Transformer for price prediction or an RL agent's environment state). This mitigates the immediate limitations of finite, noisy financial datasets.
title_cn: 数据处理不等式反映了实践吗？论低级任务的效用
summary_cn: 该研究表明，在有限样本情况下，对金融数据进行专门的预处理（如去噪、编码）可以提高分类准确率，尤其是在训练数据有限或嘈杂的真实市场环境中。这提示量化策略应重视针对性特征工程，以优化深度学习模型的信号提取效率，从而增强预测精度。

title: Atlas: Orchestrating Heterogeneous Models and Tools for Multi-Domain Complex Reasoning
summary: The integration of large language models (LLMs) with external tools has significantly expanded the capabilities of AI agents. However, as the diversity of both LLMs and tools increases, selecting the optimal model-tool combination becomes a high-dimensional optimization challenge. Existing approaches often rely on a single model or fixed tool-calling logic, failing to exploit the performance variations across heterogeneous model-tool pairs. In this paper, we present ATLAS (Adaptive Tool-LLM Alignment and Synergistic Invocation), a dual-path framework for dynamic tool usage in cross-domain complex reasoning. ATLAS operates via a dual-path approach: (1) \textbf{training-free cluster-based routing} that exploits empirical priors for domain-specific alignment, and (2) \textbf{RL-based multi-step routing} that explores autonomous trajectories for out-of-distribution generalization. Extensive experiments across 15 benchmarks demonstrate that our method outperforms closed-source models like GPT-4o, surpassing existing routing methods on both in-distribution (+10.1%) and out-of-distribution (+13.1%) tasks. Furthermore, our framework shows significant gains in visual reasoning by orchestrating specialized multi-modal tools.
core_methodology: The ATLAS framework uses a dual-path approach for selecting and orchestrating heterogeneous LLMs and external tools: (1) A training-free, cluster-based routing mechanism for domain-specific alignment based on empirical priors, and (2) An RL-based multi-step routing module for exploring optimal, out-of-distribution decision trajectories. This dynamic orchestration aims to maximize performance across various complex reasoning tasks.
data_sources: The paper focuses on general reasoning benchmarks (15 in total), implying generic textual, visual, and potentially structured data inputs for model evaluation. It is not directly using financial market data.
alpha_potential: While the paper focuses on general complex reasoning, the core concept of dynamic, adaptive orchestration of heterogeneous AI models (LLMs and specialist tools) is highly relevant for constructing sophisticated trading agents. A trading system could use ATLAS to dynamically route complex tasks—such as analyzing earnings reports (via specialized NLP tools), interpreting chart patterns (via visual tools), or optimizing portfolio allocation (via optimization algorithms)—to the best-suited model/tool combination, leading to more robust decision-making and potentially superior alpha generation compared to monolithic models.
title_cn: Atlas：为多领域复杂推理编排异构模型和工具
summary_cn: ATLAS框架通过双路径（无训练聚类路由和基于RL的多步路由）动态选择和编排异构大模型与工具，以优化复杂决策过程。该方法在金融领域可用于构建高级交易智能体，根据任务（如研报分析、市场微观结构推理）的领域特性，动态调用最合适的金融模型或工具组合，以提升策略的鲁棒性和决策质量，从而有望提高量化交易的效率和回报。

title: Noise-Driven Exploration and Transient Freezing Select Flat Minima in Stochastic Gradient Descent
summary: Stochastic gradient descent (SGD) is central to deep learning, yet the dynamical origin of its preference for flatter, more generalizable solutions remains unclear. Here, by analyzing SGD learning dynamics, we identify a nonequilibrium mechanism that governs solution selection during training. Numerical experiments reveal a transient exploratory phase in which SGD trajectories repeatedly escape sharp valleys and migrate toward flatter regions of the loss landscape before becoming confined to a final basin. Using a tractable physical model, we show that SGD noise reshapes the loss landscape into an effective potential that preferentially stabilizes flat solutions. We further uncover a transient freezing mechanism: as training progresses, the flattening landscape suppresses transitions between competing valleys. Stronger SGD noise delays this freezing transition, prolonging the exploratory phase and thereby increasing the probability of convergence to flatter minima. Together, these results provide a unified physical framework connecting learning dynamics, loss-landscape geometry, and generalization, and suggest guiding principles for the design of more effective optimization algorithms.
core_methodology: This paper develops a physical/dynamical framework to explain why Stochastic Gradient Descent (SGD) favors flatter minima in the loss landscape. The core mechanism involves analyzing transient exploration phases controlled by the noise magnitude in SGD, which sculpts an effective potential that stabilizes flatter solutions. It introduces the concept of 'transient freezing' where landscape flattening suppresses transitions between local minima as training progresses.
data_sources: The analysis is based on the optimization process of deep learning models on standard machine learning datasets (implied, as the focus is on SGD dynamics generally, not specific financial data).
alpha_potential: While the paper does not propose a trading strategy, its findings are highly relevant to the design and tuning of deep learning (DL) models used in quantitative finance, particularly in Reinforcement Learning (RL) agents, complex factor models, or microstructure prediction systems. The key practical takeaway is understanding how learning rate schedules and noise regularization (like dropping batch size or adding artificial noise) impact the generalization ability of the resulting model. Tuning these hyperparameters based on the 'transient freezing' concept could lead to models that generalize better to unseen market regimes, improving robustness in alpha generation.
title_cn: 噪声驱动的探索与瞬态冻结选择随机梯度下降中的平坦极小值
summary_cn: 该研究揭示了随机梯度下降（SGD）偏好平坦解的内在机制，通过分析噪声如何重塑损失曲面并导致“瞬态冻结”。对于量化金融应用，这提供了优化深度学习模型（如应用于因子挖掘或强化学习交易系统）的关键指导。通过调节SGD噪声（例如，通过调整学习率或批次大小），可以延长探索期，从而训练出泛化能力更强、对市场变化更稳健的交易模型，有效提升实盘表现。

title: The Implicit Bias of Steepest Descent with Mini-batch Stochastic Gradient
summary: A variety of widely used optimization methods like SignSGD and Muon can be interpreted as instances of steepest descent under different norm-induced geometries. In this work, we study the implicit bias of mini-batch stochastic steepest descent in multi-class classification, characterizing how batch size, momentum, and variance reduction shape the limiting max-margin behavior and convergence rates under general entry-wise and Schatten-$p$ norms. We show that, without momentum, worst-case convergence and successful classification can only be guaranteed with full-batch gradient. In contrast, momentum enables small-batch convergence to an approximate max-margin solution through a batch-momentum trade-off, though it slows convergence. This approach provides fully explicit, dimension-free rates that improve upon prior results. Moreover, we prove that variance reduction can recover the exact full-batch implicit bias for any batch size, albeit at a slower convergence rate. Finally, we further investigate the batch-size-one steepest descent without momentum, and reveal its convergence to a fundamentally different bias via a concrete data example, which reveals a key limitation of purely stochastic updates. Overall, our unified analysis clarifies when stochastic optimization aligns with full-batch behavior, and paves the way for perform deeper explorations of the training behavior of stochastic gradient steepest descent algorithms.
core_methodology: The paper analyzes the implicit bias of mini-batch Stochastic Steepest Descent (SSD) optimization algorithms, examining how batch size, momentum, and variance reduction influence convergence rates and the resulting solution (e.g., max-margin behavior). It provides explicit, dimension-free convergence rates for these optimization techniques under different norms.
data_sources: The analysis is theoretical and relies on mathematical frameworks applicable to generic optimization problems, conceptually mapping to models trained on financial time series or order book data.
alpha_potential: This research provides foundational knowledge for training high-performance machine learning models used in quantitative trading. Understanding how mini-batch optimization parameters (like batch size and momentum) affect the model's convergence to specific solutions (like max-margin classifiers or robust regression estimators) is crucial for designing stable and effective trading algorithms. Insights on when stochastic updates diverge from full-batch behavior can inform the robustness of models trained on noisy financial data.
title_cn: 随机梯度下降的隐性偏差：小批量与最优下降法的分析
summary_cn: 该研究深入分析了随机梯度下降（SSD）优化方法中，小批量、动量和方差缩减如何影响模型收敛和最终解的性质。这对于设计和优化用于金融预测的深度学习模型至关重要，帮助量化研究人员选择最佳训练参数，以提高策略的稳定性和泛化能力，尤其是在处理高噪声市场数据时。

title: Position: Modular Memory is the Key to Continual Learning Agents
summary: Foundation models have transformed machine learning through large-scale pretraining and increased test-time compute. Despite surpassing human performance in several domains, these models remain fundamentally limited in continuous operation, experience accumulation, and personalization, capabilities that are central to adaptive intelligence. While continual learning research has long targeted these goals, its historical focus on in-weight learning (IWL), i.e., updating a single model's parameters to absorb new knowledge, has rendered catastrophic forgetting a persistent challenge. Our position is that combining the strengths of In-Weight Learning (IWL) and the newly emerged capabilities of In-Context Learning (ICL) through the design of modular memory is the missing piece for continual adaptation at scale. We outline a conceptual framework for modular memory-centric architectures that leverage ICL for rapid adaptation and knowledge accumulation, and IWL for stable updates to model capabilities, charting a practical roadmap toward continually learning agents.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a conceptual framework for continual learning agents by integrating In-Weight Learning (IWL) and In-Context Learning (ICL) via modular memory architectures to overcome catastrophic forgetting in foundation models.
data_sources: The paper discusses general machine learning paradigms, implying application potential to time-series financial data, market states, and institutional knowledge bases.
alpha_potential: This research addresses the fundamental challenge of adapting large AI models to dynamic financial environments without retraining from scratch. A successful modular memory system could enable trading agents to continuously learn from new market regimes, adapt to unforeseen events (black swans), and personalize strategies for specific assets or mandates, leading to more robust and persistent alpha generation.
title_cn: 位置：模块化记忆是持续学习智能体的关键
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种结合权值学习（IWL）和上下文学习（ICL）的模块化记忆框架，以解决大型模型在持续学习中的灾难性遗忘问题。这对于量化交易具有重要意义，因为它能使交易智能体在不断变化的市场环境中快速适应新信息和市场结构，同时保留关键知识，从而构建比静态模型更具鲁棒性和适应性的持续盈利策略。

title: Adaptive Domain Models: Bayesian Evolution, Warm Rotation, and Principled Training for Geometric and Neuromorphic AI
summary: Prevailing AI training assumes reverse-mode automatic differentiation over IEEE-754 arithmetic. The memory overhead of training relative to inference, optimizer complexity, and structural degradation of geometric properties through training are consequences of this arithmetic substrate. This paper develops an alternative training architecture grounded in three prior results: the Dimensional Type System and Deterministic Memory Management framework (Haynes 2026), which establishes stack-eligible gradient allocation and exact quire accumulation as design-time verifiable properties; the Program Hypergraph (Haynes 2026), which establishes grade preservation through geometric algebra computations as a type-level invariant; and the b-posit bounded-regime design (Jonnalagadda et al. 2025), which makes posit arithmetic tractable across hardware targets conventionally considered inference-only. Their composition enables depth-independent training memory bounded to approximately twice the inference footprint, grade-preserving weight updates, and exact gradient accumulation, applicable uniformly to loss-function-optimized and spike-timing-dependent neuromorphic models. We introduce *Bayesian distillation*, a mechanism by which the latent prior structure of a general-purpose model is extracted through the ADM training regime, resolving the data-scarcity bootstrapping problem for domain-specific training. For deployment, we introduce *warm rotation*, an operational pattern in which an updated model transitions into an active inference pathway without service interruption, with correctness formalized through PHG certificates and signed version records. The result is a class of domain-specific AI systems that are smaller and more precise than general-purpose models, continuously adaptive, verifiably correct with respect to the physical structure of their domains, and initializable from existing models.
core_methodology: The paper introduces an alternative AI training architecture that moves away from standard reverse-mode automatic differentiation (AD) over IEEE-754 arithmetic. It leverages specific prior frameworks (Dimensional Type System, Program Hypergraph) and posit arithmetic (b-posit) to achieve memory-efficient, grade-preserving training. Key mechanisms include 'Bayesian distillation' for domain-specific adaptation and 'warm rotation' for interruption-free model deployment.
data_sources: The paper focuses on the AI training framework itself, rather than specific financial data sources. However, the methods are generalized for geometric and neuromorphic models, suggesting applicability to time series data, high-frequency data, or alternative data where model precision and efficiency are critical.
alpha_potential: The primary alpha potential stems from the ability to train significantly smaller, more precise, and continuously adaptive domain-specific models efficiently. This could enable the deployment of complex models (potentially including deep reinforcement learning or structured prediction models in high-frequency environments) where standard GPU memory overhead and latency were previously prohibitive. The verifiability and precision gains from using posit arithmetic and geometric substrate preservation might lead to more robust and less error-prone predictions in complex market prediction tasks.
title_cn: 自适应域模型：贝叶斯蒸馏、热旋转和面向几何与神经形态AI的原则性训练
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种新的AI训练范式，使用非标准算术（如posit）和几何保护机制，极大降低了训练的内存和计算开销。对于量化交易，这意味着可以在资源受限的边缘设备或高频系统中部署更精确、更小的、能持续适应市场结构变化的定制模型。其'热旋转'机制保障了模型无中断更新，提升了策略的实时性和稳健性。

title: Decidable By Construction: Design-Time Verification for Trustworthy AI
summary: A prevailing assumption in machine learning is that model correctness must be enforced after the fact. We observe that the properties determining whether an AI model is numerically stable, computationally correct, or consistent with a physical domain do not necessarily demand post hoc enforcement. They can be verified at design time, before training begins, at marginal computational cost, with particular relevance to models deployed in high-leverage decision support and scientifically constrained settings. These properties share a specific algebraic structure: they are expressible as constraints over finitely generated abelian groups $\mathbb{Z}^n$, where inference is decidable in polynomial time and the principal type is unique. A framework built on this observation composes three prior results (arXiv:2603.16437, arXiv:2603.17627, arXiv:2603.18104): a dimensional type system carrying arbitrary annotations as persistent codata through model elaboration; a program hypergraph that infers Clifford algebra grade and derives geometric product sparsity from type signatures alone; and an adaptive domain model architecture preserving both invariants through training via forward-mode coeffect analysis and exact posit accumulation. We believe this composition yields a novel information-theoretic result: Hindley-Milner unification over abelian groups computes the maximum a posteriori hypothesis under a computable restriction of Solomonoff's universal prior, placing the framework's type inference on the same formal ground as universal induction. We compare four contemporary approaches to AI reliability and show that each imposes overhead that can compound across deployments, layers, and inference requests. This framework eliminates that overhead by construction.
core_methodology: The paper proposes a design-time verification framework for AI models, focusing on algebraic structures (constraints over finitely generated abelian groups $\mathbb{Z}^n$) to ensure numerical stability and correctness *before* training. It leverages type systems, program hypergraphs, and adaptive domain models combined with forward-mode coeffect analysis and exact posit accumulation.
data_sources: The framework applies to the structural properties of the AI models themselves, not specific financial data. The resulting verified models could be applied to any data source (time series, order book data, etc.).
alpha_potential: While not a direct trading strategy, the framework allows for the construction and deployment of highly robust, verifiable, and computationally efficient ML/AI models for trading applications. By guaranteeing correctness and stability at design time, it significantly reduces deployment risk for high-leverage strategies built on complex models (e.g., deep reinforcement learning agents or high-frequency microstructure models). The elimination of post-hoc verification overhead can lead to faster inference and more reliable decision-making.
title_cn: 构造可知：面向可信赖人工智能的设计时验证
summary_cn: 该论文提出了一种AI模型设计时验证框架，确保数值稳定性和计算正确性，尤其适用于高杠杆决策场景。通过基于阿贝尔群的代数结构约束和独特的类型系统，该方法在训练前即可排除错误。这使量化交易团队能够构建和部署更可靠、更高效的AI驱动策略，显著降低模型部署后的风险，并可能提升高频交易中的计算效率。

title: Conditional Attribution for Root Cause Analysis in Time-Series Anomaly Detection
summary: Root cause analysis (RCA) for time-series anomaly detection is critical for the reliable operation of complex real-world systems. Existing explanation methods often rely on unrealistic feature perturbations and ignore temporal and cross-feature dependencies, leading to unreliable attributions. We propose a conditional attribution framework that explains anomalies relative to contextually similar normal system states. Instead of using marginal or randomly sampled baselines, our method retrieves representative normal instances conditioned on the anomalous observation, enabling dependency-preserving and operationally meaningful explanations. To support high-dimensional time-series data, contextual retrieval is performed in learned low-dimensional representations using both variational autoencoder latent spaces and UMAP manifold embeddings. By grounding the retrieval process in the system's learned manifold, this strategy avoids out-of-distribution artifacts and ensures attribution fidelity while maintaining computational efficiency. We further introduce confidence-aware and temporal evaluation metrics for assessing explanation reliability and responsiveness. Experiments on the SWaT and MSDS benchmarks demonstrate that the proposed approach consistently improves root-cause identification accuracy, temporal localization, and robustness across multiple anomaly detection models. These results highlight the practical utility of conditional attribution for explainable anomaly diagnosis in complex time-series systems. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/dfki-av/Conditional-Attribution-for-Root-Cause-Analysis-in-Time-Series-Anomaly-Detection.
core_methodology: The core methodology involves a conditional attribution framework for Root Cause Analysis (RCA) in time-series anomaly detection. It establishes 'normal' contexts by retrieving representative normal instances conditioned on the anomalous observation, contrasting with methods that use unrealistic or marginal baselines. This retrieval is computationally efficient, utilizing learned low-dimensional representations from Variational Autoencoders (VAEs) and UMAP embeddings to preserve temporal and cross-feature dependencies.
data_sources: The paper focuses on high-dimensional time-series data for system anomaly detection, exemplified by industrial control system benchmarks (SWaT and MSDS). In a financial context, this would map to high-frequency market data, order book dynamics, tick data, or extensive sets of correlated macroeconomic or alternative data streams.
alpha_potential: The direct application is in anomaly detection within complex financial systems (e.g., high-frequency trading infrastructure or market surveillance). While not a direct alpha generation strategy, robust RCA for anomalies is critical for operational stability and risk management. A strong RCA capability can help in rapidly diagnosing system failures that might cause temporary alpha decay or unexpected slippage, thus preserving PnL. Furthermore, applying this methodology to detect structural market anomalies (which might signal regime changes or arbitrage opportunities) after conditioning on the 'normal' market state could lead to novel signal generation.
title_cn: 时间序列异常检测中的条件归因用于根本原因分析
summary_cn: 该研究提出了一种用于时间序列异常检测的条件归因框架，用于可靠的根本原因分析（RCA）。通过在学习到的低维空间中检索与异常情景相似的正常状态，该方法能提供保留依赖关系且更具操作意义的解释。在金融交易中，这可用于快速诊断交易系统或市场数据的异常根源，增强系统鲁棒性，并可能用于识别关键的市场结构性异常信号。

title: Weisfeiler Lehman Test on Combinatorial Complexes: Generalized Expressive Power of Topological Neural Networks
summary: Topological neural networks have emerged as effective tools for modeling higher-order relational structures beyond pairwise graphs, including hypergraphs, simplicial complexes, and cell complexes. However, existing Weisfeiler-Leman type expressivity analyses are typically developed on different structural domains and rely on domain-specific neighborhood systems, making their expressive powers difficult to compare within a common formalism. In this paper, we introduce the Combinatorial Complex Weisfeiler-Leman (CCWL) framework, a unified expressive power refinement defined on combinatorial complexes. By exploiting the ability of combinatorial complexes to represent both set-type relations and part-whole hierarchies, CCWL performs topological color refinement through four structural neighborhoods: boundary, co-boundary, lower adjacency, and upper adjacency. We show that, under specified lifting maps, CCWL can simulate several domain-specific WL-type refinements, thereby providing a common theoretical baseline for analyzing topological message passing. We further study the neighborhood sufficiency problem and prove that, under explicit coverage conditions, a reduced refinement using only lower- and upper-adjacent bridge information preserves the distinguishing power of the full four-neighborhood CCWL refinement. Guided by this theoretical result, we instantiate the reduced refinement as the Combinatorial Complex Isomorphism Network (CCIN). Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmarks demonstrate that CCIN achieves competitive performance against representative graph and topological neural network baselines. Ablation studies and resource-efficiency analyses further support the effectiveness of the proposed lower/upper-neighborhood design.
core_methodology: The paper introduces the Combinatorial Complex Weisfeiler-Leman (CCWL) framework and the resulting Combinatorial Complex Isomorphism Network (CCIN). This methodology unifies and refines the expressive power analysis of Topological Neural Networks (TNNs) by utilizing four structural neighborhoods (boundary, co-boundary, lower adjacency, upper adjacency) within combinatorial complexes. The key insight is that a reduced refinement using only lower- and upper-adjacent bridge information maintains distinguishing power.
data_sources: Synthetic benchmarks and unspecified 'real-world benchmarks'. In a financial context, the data would likely be market graphs (e.g., inter-stock correlation graphs, supply chain networks, high-frequency trade flows, or derivatives pricing structures) represented as higher-order topological structures (simplicial or cell complexes).
alpha_potential: The primary value is providing a robust, theoretically grounded framework (CCIN) for accurately comparing and modeling complex relational structures beyond standard pairwise graphs. In finance, this is crucial for modeling intricate market interconnectedness (e.g., systemic risk factors, sector contagions, or complex derivative relationships). A model capable of better capturing these higher-order topologies could lead to superior predictive signals for systemic market movements or factor exposures, thus improving portfolio optimization and arbitrage strategies.
title_cn: 组合复形上的Weisfeiler-Lehman测试：拓扑神经网络的广义表达能力
summary_cn: 该研究提出了组合复形上的CCWL框架和CCIN模型，能有效分析和建模超越传统图结构的高阶复杂关联。在金融应用中，CCIN可用于更精确地刻画市场中跨资产、供应链或衍生品网络等高阶拓扑结构。这有助于捕获更深层的系统性风险和因子间关系，从而优化投资组合和挖掘基于市场复杂性的潜在阿尔法信号。

title: A Recipe for Long-Context Reasoning in Large Language Models via On-Policy Optimization and Distillation
summary: Existing approaches to post-train models for long-context tasks face complementary limitations: (i) supervised fine-tuning (SFT) provides stable supervision but suffers from exposure bias; (ii) reinforcement learning methods such as Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) train on model-generated trajectories but struggle with long-horizon credit assignment and sparse rewards; and (iii) on-policy distillation (OPD) provides dense token-level guidance but does not directly optimize task rewards. We study these complementary strategies for long-context alignment and derive a recipe that combines GRPO with OPD-style teacher guidance: the student learns from its own rollouts using outcome-level rewards, while a stronger teacher provides dense token-level regularization in place of the standard reference policy. This is especially useful when process-level supervision is difficult to obtain. To support this study, we introduce LongBlocks, a synthetic multilingual dataset spanning multi-hop reasoning, contextual grounding, and long-form generation. Through controlled ablations, we isolate the roles of cold-start initialization, teacher anchoring, and data mixing, showing that our recipe yields a more stable and effective path to long-context reasoning than GRPO or OPD while preserving short-context capabilities.
core_methodology: The paper introduces a novel hybrid training recipe combining Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with On-Policy Distillation (OPD) style teacher guidance. This method optimizes the student model using outcome-level rewards derived from its own long-context rollouts while simultaneously regularizing token-level predictions using dense guidance from a stronger teacher model. This addresses credit assignment issues in RL for long sequences.
data_sources: The paper introduces LongBlocks, a synthetic multilingual dataset designed for multi-hop reasoning and long-context tasks. While synthetic, the methodology is designed to be dataset-agnostic and applicable to real-world long-context financial data.
alpha_potential: The primary value is in developing more robust and effective Large Language Models (LLMs) capable of complex, long-horizon reasoning and synthesizing vast amounts of sequential financial text (e.g., earning call transcripts, regulatory filings, complex news narratives).
